title: Lambda Expressions

sections.markdown: A lambda is an anonymous function you can pass around. It implements a **functional interface** (exactly one abstract method) concisely.
Lambdas capture **effectively final** local variables (you can't reassign them). They don't introduce a new scope for `this` — `this` refers to the enclosing instance, unlike anonymous classes.
Prefer method references (String::toUpperCase) when they read clearly; fall back to lambdas for logic. Keep lambdas short — extract to a named method if they grow.

flashcards.back: An interface with exactly one abstract method (e.g. Runnable, Comparator), targetable by a lambda.

flashcards.front: Function vs Predicate vs Consumer vs Supplier?
flashcards.back: Function transforms (T→R), Predicate tests (T→boolean), Consumer accepts (T→void), Supplier produces (→T).

flashcards.front: What variables can a lambda capture?
flashcards.back: Effectively final locals — variables not reassigned after initialization.

quiz.explain: Lambdas target functional interfaces with a single abstract method.

quiz.q: Lambdas can capture locals that are…
quiz.explain: Captured locals must be effectively final.
